records.text: The Middle East contains sharply different demographic structures, from young and rapidly growing populations to ageing high-income states; demographic heterogeneity must be preserved.

records.source: World Bank MENAAP Economic Update Oct 2026
records.text: Regional output is projected to contract in 2026 because conflict and disrupted energy/trade routes hit oil production, tourism, aviation and logistics, while some developing oil importers remain more resilient.

Strategic oil and logistics infrastructure, including East-West rerouting capacity, materially reduced losses from shipping disruption, showing functioning regional transport/energy-routing infrastructure.
MENA had 308 million mobile internet users and accelerating 5G adoption, with Gulf economies investing heavily in AI, data and digital infrastructure, although readiness remains highly uneven.

records.source: World Bank / IMF 2026 Middle East conflict assessments
records.text: The near closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupted energy exports, tourism, aviation and logistics, demonstrating strong dependence on maritime chokepoints and external trade routes.
Buna operates as a centralized cross-border, multi-currency payment and settlement system supported by Arab central banks, providing a functioning regional financial carrier.
The 2026 Middle East war generated severe regional energy, transport, trade and inflation shocks, including large disruptions to Hormuz traffic and supply chains.
AI adoption is advancing at very different speeds across the region, with Gulf economies moving fastest while fragile economies still face foundational electricity and connectivity gaps.
records.reason: Supports transition/reconfiguration context but not a mature cross-region P3 mechanism.

conflictsAndUnknowns: Middle East regional aggregates mask large differences between GCC oil exporters, oil importers and conflict-affected economies.
Buna covers the Arab region and is used as a bounded regional financial-carrier observation, not proof of uniform use across every Middle Eastern economy.
War-related disruptions are current shocks and do not by themselves establish permanent continuity semantics.
